title: Lebanese Chicken Shish Platter
seoTitle: Lebanese Chicken Shish Platter | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Garlic-lemon chicken skewers with toum and tabbouleh for ten
subtitle: Garlic-lemon chicken skewers with toum and tabbouleh for ten
description: Chicken breast chunks marinate in lemon, garlic, yogurt, and olive oil, then grill on skewers until charred at the edges. Serve with toum garlic sauce, tabbouleh, pickles, and warm pita.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Lebanese Chicken Shish Platter in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Marinate chicken
steps.instruction: Mix lemon juice, olive oil, yogurt, minced garlic, paprika, salt, and pepper. Coat chicken and marinate at least 2 hours. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Make toum
steps.instruction: Blend garlic with lemon juice, then slowly stream in oil until thick and fluffy like mayonnaise. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Prep tabbouleh
steps.instruction: Soak bulgur in hot water 20 minutes, drain, and toss with parsley, diced tomato, cucumber, mint, lemon, and olive oil. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill skewers
steps.instruction: Thread chicken onto skewers. Grill over medium-high heat 10–12 minutes until charred and 165°F internal. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Platter and serve
steps.instruction: Arrange skewers on platters with tabbouleh, toum, pickles, and warm pita. Slide chicken off skewers at the line if preferred. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Sumac on finished chicken adds classic Lebanese tang.
Pickled turnips from a jar are worth buying for authenticity.
If toum breaks, blend in another egg white to re-emulsify.
tonightSpread: Shish taouk with toum, tabbouleh, pickles, and warm pita.
Hummus on the side for double-dip energy.
leftovers: Chicken in pita with toum and pickles for lunch.
Tabbouleh holds 2 days—good side for next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Shish taouk is Mediterranean comfort without the pasta or rice-bowl rut. Garlic-lemon chicken on skewers feels like a backyard cookout with better seasoning, and toum separates the rookies from crews who respect raw garlic.
mealPrepNotes: Yogurt marinade tenderizes breast meat—do not skip. Make toum in a food processor ahead. Tabbouleh improves if parsley is chopped fine and salad rests 30 minutes.
